# An actual M-object not cogenerated by any of the V^R templates

2026-11-18. Status: PROOF_RECONSTRUCTED; independently checked by a second research agent, not externally reviewed or formally verified. This is a ZFC obstruction to extending the protected V-template equalizer results by a cogeneration argument. It is not an equalizer counterexample and does not settle Problem 4.

Use c=2^aleph_0, lambda=c^+, and the original scalar monic union

    K=colim_(alpha<omega_1) omega^(T_alpha)

from the coinfinite-injection construction. Its stages are monic, each |T_alpha|<=c, and each T_alpha is nonempty. For R in the diagram category, put

    V^R=colim_(alpha<omega_1) E(T_alpha·R).

## 1. A tail quotient that is in the actual M

Let Z_*=(omega --id,id--> omega), which lies in C. Define

    U=colim_(beta<lambda) E([beta,lambda)·Z_*),

using tail restriction maps. The [bounded-template tail theorem](mono_candidate_tail_quotients_2026-11-18.md) applies: Z_* has countable carriers, and lambda>c. Therefore U belongs to the actual mono-factorization class M, in ZFC.

In either sort, U_i is the M_2-set of germs of functions [beta,lambda)×omega→omega, with equality on a later tail. The constant-zero and constant-one germs are distinct, so U_i is nontrivial.

There is an M_2-map

    j:omega^lambda→U_i

given by functions constant in the omega-coordinate, j(f)=[(t,r)↦f(t)]. Functions differing only on a bounded subset of lambda have the same image under j.

## 2. Two ZFC properties of maps from powers into K

The following facts were proved directly in Sections 2–3 of
[the scalar kernel note](nonstage_scalar_maps_require_inner_measurable_2026-11-18.md). They do not use its later no-inner-measurable assumption.

For any M_2-map psi:omega^S→K, finite tuple coding gives a Boolean homomorphism

    psi_B:P(S)→B_K,

where B_K is the Boolean part of K. Its kernel ideal I is c^+-complete. To see the completeness, partition S into at most c blocks and precompose psi with omega^Q→omega^S, where Q is the block set. The small-index ZFC scalar theorem makes this composite an actual stage evaluation. It therefore preserves the join of those blocks. Disjointifying at most c kernel sets proves that their union remains in I.

Also, B_K has cellularity at most c. Assign each member of an antichain to a stage containing it. At one stage its representatives are pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets of T_alpha, so there are at most c of them. There are omega_1<=c stages.

These are the only scalar facts needed below; the arbitrary-index stage-factorization theorem under no inner measurable cardinal is not used.

## 3. No scalar map U_i→K exists

**Theorem (ZFC).** Hom_(M_2)(U_i,K)=empty for both sorts i.

Suppose phi:U_i→K exists. Compose with j to obtain psi:omega^lambda→K, and let I⊂P(lambda) be its Boolean kernel ideal. By Section 2, I is c^+-complete and P(lambda)/I has cellularity at most c. It is proper because psi preserves the distinct Boolean constants 0 and 1.

Every bounded subset A⊂lambda belongs to I: its characteristic function has the same j-image as the zero function. We now give a direct Ulam-matrix contradiction.

For every beta<lambda=c^+, choose an injection

    e_beta:beta→c.

For alpha<lambda and i<c define

    A_(alpha,i)={beta>alpha : e_beta(alpha)=i}.

For fixed alpha these c sets partition the tail {beta>alpha}, whose I-class is 1 because its complement is bounded. Since I is closed under c unions, at least one A_(alpha,i) is I-positive. Choose such an i=i_alpha.

There are lambda many alpha and only c possible i. Hence some fixed i is chosen for lambda many alpha. For distinct such alpha,alpha', the sets A_(alpha,i) and A_(alpha',i) are disjoint: a common beta would violate injectivity of e_beta.

We have produced lambda=c^+ pairwise disjoint I-positive sets. Their images form an antichain of size c^+ in P(lambda)/I, contradicting cellularity at most c. Therefore phi cannot exist. □

## 4. No product of V-templates can receive a monomorphism from U

For every r∈R_i, evaluation at r gives an M_2-map

    (V^R)_i→K.

If R_i is nonempty, any P-map U→V^R would compose to an M_2-map U_i→K, which Section 3 excludes. Thus

    Hom_P(U,V^R)=empty

for every nonempty diagram R. For the empty diagram R, the object V^R is terminal.

Consequently U cannot embed in a set-indexed product of objects V^R. If any factor has nonempty R, even a map to the product is impossible. If all factors have empty R, the product is terminal, and U is not subterminal because its componentwise 0 and 1 are distinct.

This holds in ZFC and therefore also under V=L or the stronger scalar stage-factorization hypotheses. It shows that the entire family of V^R, even allowing arbitrarily large R, does not cogenerate the actual M.

The protected equalizer results for codomains embedding in products of V^R remain valid. The proposed extension that every M-object admits such an embedding is false, witnessed by this explicit U∈M.
